about: What real use, and the person Pit Board is for, showed must change or must stay true in Windstorm Pit Board, and the version each is due in. A lesson here is a gate, not a note: tests/test_g21_promises.py (G21.14) refuses a version while a row due in it is not built, and refuses the version after it until the row says where it was proven on a real machine.
how_to_use: A new lesson gets a row the day it is learned: what was seen, the promise, a codon in DNA-STRAND-MASTER-PLAN.md, the version it is due in, and a tracking issue when work is left.
When it is built: put the name of its test in 'test'. The test must exist under tests/ and be named with the row's codon (test_G10_5_... for G10.5).
When it has been seen to work on a real machine: say which machine, which version and when in 'proven'.

'ship_in' moves only with a reason in 'moved_why'. A row whose owner is 'person' was seen by the person Pit Board is for, on their own machine: its date moves only by their word, restated in 'moved_by_person'.
A row is never deleted. A promise that turns out wrong is closed by a row that says why.
A lesson that was heard and not taken goes under 'declined' with the reason, so that nothing is dropped without a word.

rows.promise: Pit Board's status segment is printed first: before a one-line status line, joined with ' · ', or on its own first line above a status line of several lines, so a long status line never hides it.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, the first night Pit Board was installed in single lanes' folders on two test machines (a shared Linux laptop and an Intel Mac): a machine with no Pit Board home could get one from pitboard setup --minimal --apply only together with a change to the user's own statusLine setting, which reaches every session of that user. The folder installer had to make the home itself, without that step.
rows.promise: pitboard setup has a folder mode: it makes the Pit Board home and sets the status line wrapper in one folder's .claude/settings.local.json, never in the user's settings, and its undo puts that file back byte for byte (or removes only Pit Board's entries if the file changed since).
rows.proven: 2026-11-22, the overnight stress test, setup --folder from the folder mode on main with Claude Code 2.1.330's real plugin commands: on a shared Linux laptop (bash) and on an Intel Mac (zsh), the main user, apply then undo left the folder empty, the registry with no entry for it and the user's settings.json byte for byte the same; on a fresh macOS test account with no Pit Board home, apply made the home (config, launcher, wrapper) without the user's status line setting and the undo left the folder empty; and in a folder another skill had changed after the install, the undo removed only Pit Board's entries and kept the other skill's env and backup file.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, the same night, on the Intel Mac: pgrep -x claude sees a Claude Code session's process name as its version file (2.1.330), so counting the sessions in a folder by process name could find none, and a refusal of a folder shared by several sessions would never fire.
rows.promise: The folder mode counts the sessions in a folder by each process's command name, on Linux and macOS, and refuses the home folder and any folder where more than one session runs.
rows.proven: 2026-11-22, the overnight stress test: on an Intel Mac, where a session's process name is its version file, the folder mode counted exactly one session in each of three test folders that each held one (and the same on a shared Linux laptop), and refused the home folder on both.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, round 2 of the overnight stress test, a clean reboot of an Intel Mac: a session whose Pit Board home was chosen by PITBOARD_HOME in its start environment was brought back by a session restorer without that variable (the restorer carries only the variables it is told to). Its hooks then wrote to the default home, so its start-up reminder said nothing was open while its ask was open, and an answer typed there would have gone to the wrong home. Its status line still showed the ask, because the wrapper names its own home: the two halves disagreed without a word.
rows.promise: A Pit Board home other than the default is set in the folder's own settings (env.PITBOARD_HOME, written by setup --folder), not only in a session's start environment, so a session brought back by any tool keeps its home.
rows.proven: 2026-11-22T07:35Z, round 3b of the overnight stress test, an ungraceful quick restart of an Intel Mac: the session's folder had env.PITBOARD_HOME set by setup --folder (the folder mode on main, 0.1.0 hooks from the catalog) and its process environment had none. The restorer resumed it, and its hooks found the chosen home: the start-up reminder listed its open ask, and the default home got no line from it. Then on the 0.1.1 candidate itself, installed from its commit (cf0391e) into the session's folder with setup --folder: on the same Mac, a session started new by the restorer with no PITBOARD_HOME in its environment found its home after clean reboots at 09:45Z and 11:15Z; and on a shared Linux laptop (bash), the session resumed at 12:14Z, after a sudden reset (12:26Z) and after two clean reboots (12:51Z and 12:53Z), each time with no PITBOARD_HOME in its process environment: its hooks wrote to the chosen home, the start-up reminder listed its open ask, and the default home got no line from it.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, the overnight stress test, an Intel Mac: one test folder had the 0.1.1 candidate installed from its commit with setup --folder and its own Pit Board home, while other test folders on the machine had 0.1.0. The plugin's own bin/pitboard in that folder ran 0.1.1, but the home's stable launcher, which the status line wrapper calls, ran 0.1.0: no version is in update/good-versions before the self-check of G21.3 exists, so G21.4 step 6 took the first entry in installed_plugins.json, whatever its version. No effect in 0.1.1, whose status line and hook code are those of 0.1.0. The fix (G21.4 step 6, plan 1.15) was seen on a real Intel Mac test account on 2026-11-22 at 15:37Z, Claude Code 2.1.330: two folders, each with its own local-scope catalog, the 0.1.0 release installed first and the fixed code (0.1.1) second, and a Pit Board home with no self-check yet. The 0.1.1 release's stable launcher ran 0.1.0 ("0.1.0 (installed 0.1.1, hooks gen 1)"), and the fixed one ran 0.1.1. Still to see before 0.1.2's tag: a home set up by 0.1.0 or 0.1.1 whose stable copy the first session start of a folder on 0.1.2 refreshes (plan 1.16), so its status line runs the new launcher; and a restore of ten or more sessions of one home on a real machine that leaves one whole copy.
rows.promise: Before any version has passed a self-check, the stable launcher runs the highest installed version, not the first one listed, so the status line never runs code older than the newest install.
rows.proven: 2026-11-22 on an Intel Mac test machine, Claude Code 2.1.330, the 0.1.2 candidate (main at edda023b, the refresh code, with version 0.1.2) installed in every test folder from a git source, three sightings, each for what it is. (1) The refresh of an old home by the real upgrade path: a Pit Board home set up by 0.1.1's own `setup --folder`, whose copy answered '0.1.0 (installed 0.1.2, hooks gen 1)', got its first session start on 0.1.2 at a clean reboot's restore (18:05:07Z); its log then said 'stable launcher before-0.1.2 -> 0.1.2, backup kept', and its copy answered '0.1.2 (installed 0.1.2, hooks gen 1)', with `.prev` equal to 0.1.1's launcher, no leftovers, and the status line wrapper running through it. (2) A ten-session restore of one home on the same reboot, NOT simultaneous: the restore tool started the ten sessions about 5 s apart (18:05:12Z to 18:05:56Z, load about 86 at the end of the restore), the first hook refreshed the copy in 1.4 s and the other nine found it current; one whole copy was left, checked as in (1). (3) Ten real session-start hooks of one home at the same moment, at 19:21:46Z under load 39.8, 67.2 and 78.9 (1, 5 and 15 minutes): a home set up by 0.1.1's own setup code, ten hooks from the candidate's installed version folder in the plugin cache, released within 0.3 ms; up to 10 refresh folders existed at once and all ten exited 0 with their SessionStart output. Six refreshed the copy; four stopped at the 3 s check under the load and wrote nothing. At the end: one whole copy (the candidate's files, copied-from 0.1.2), `.prev` equal to 0.1.1's, no leftovers, and the copy answered '0.1.2 (installed 0.1.2, hooks gen 1)'. The same race runs in CI on Linux and macOS (tests/test_g21_stablecopy.py, twelve hooks).

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, round 6 of the overnight stress test, a clean reboot of an Intel Mac in the middle of the work: in a fresh macOS test account, setup --folder --apply and --undo ran in a loop. 7 of 28 installs failed in claude plugin install while it cloned the plugin (once before the reboot, 6 times as the network went down). Each failed apply undid itself and left the folder clean (G18.1 step 6), but the message kept only the last line of Claude Code's error: 'claude plugin install failed: and the repository exists.; undone'. Later the same day, the skill's owner's install from the catalog in a clean test account (Claude Code 2.1.280, no GitHub key) failed with 'Host key verification failed' and 'Permission denied (publickey)': the clone went over SSH. A fresh macOS test account with no GitHub key (Claude Code 2.1.330) had installed over HTTPS 21 times; its one passing failure said 'HTTPS clone failed, retrying with SSH'. The real output of both failed clones, recorded with no terminal as setup runs it, is kept in tests/fixtures/claude_plugin_errors and replayed by the row's test.
rows.promise: When a claude plugin command fails, setup --folder shows Claude Code's error from its first error line to its end, not only its last line. When that error shows the clone failed over SSH because GitHub accepted no key ('Host key verification failed' or 'Permission denied (publickey)'), it says so first, in plain words: Claude Code could not clone the plugin from GitHub over SSH; this account is not set up for GitHub over SSH (GitHub accepted no key from it). Then what to do: check that this machine reaches github.com over HTTPS, or add a GitHub key to this account, and run the same setup --folder again.
rows.proven: 2026-11-22T14:37Z, the code of commit 527ba6c run for real in two test accounts with no GitHub key, each in a scratch folder whose own catalog held a github entry it could not clone: setup --folder --apply exited 6, put the folder back, and showed the plain-words lines first, then Claude Code's whole error, every line within 100 columns and none cut. Claude Code 2.1.280 on Linux (the real Pit Board entry, cloned over SSH only): the SSH form. Claude Code 2.1.330 on an Intel Mac (an entry for a repository that does not exist, so HTTPS failed first): the HTTPS-then-SSH form, with Claude Code's own advice line, and its progress lines left out.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, the overnight stress test, an Intel Mac after an uninstall and reinstall round: four test folders had 0.1.0 from the catalog and one had the 0.1.1 candidate. Every home's stable launcher (the status line) ran 0.1.1, while the hooks in a 0.1.0 folder ran that folder's 0.1.0. Removing a version from one folder would not move the status line back while another folder still has it, and 0.1.x has no command to choose a version (G21.10's pin comes with the updater).
rows.promise: A person can hold a Pit Board home on a version they choose, and release it, with one command (pitboard self-update --pin VER and --unpin), before the rest of the updater exists; pitboard version names the pin.
rows.proven: 2026-11-22 at 16:07Z on a Linux test account, Claude Code 2.1.280, code f9cba870 (plans 1.15 and 1.18): two folders with git-source installs, the 0.1.0 release and the P10 code (0.1.1), and a Pit Board home whose stable launcher copy came from the P10 code. Before: the status line's launcher and the newer folder's own launcher (the hooks' path) both ran 0.1.1. `self-update --pin 0.1.0` exited 0 with "0.1.1 (installed 0.1.1, pinned 0.1.0, hooks gen 1)"; then both launchers ran 0.1.0 and a status line call exited 0. `self-update --unpin` through the stable copy, though 0.1.0 has no self-update, exited 0 with "0.1.1 (installed 0.1.1, hooks gen 1)", and both launchers ran 0.1.1 again. `--pin 9.9.9` and a bare `update` were refused, the pin unchanged. Everything undone.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, a check asked of every Windstorm skill after a sister skill's row test had never run anywhere: the promise gate found a row's test by its name as text in the test files. A row's real test (due in the version then in plugin.json) was moved six ways where it cannot run, each in a throwaway copy: the gate refused three (under a helper after its return, renamed, under if False) and PASSED three while the real test never ran (marked skip; shadowed by a later empty definition of the same name, which the runner passes under that name; inside a module string). The gate also checked a row only once the version reached its due version, so on 0.1.1 the tests of P8, P9 and P10, due in 0.1.2, were not checked at all.
rows.promise: The promise gate counts a row's test only when the test runner collects it and runs it to a pass in this checkout, from the runner's own report, for every row that names a test at every version. A name defined twice in one file, an unconditional skip and a skip with no reason fail; a skip on a condition of the machine is listed as not run here and is not a pass.
rows.proven: 2026-11-22, CI's own logs on main (GitHub's hosted runners, Linux and macOS, Python 3.10 and 3.13). Run 45085025204 on the merge commit 8ffb227d, where this gate and its self-tests first ran, completed with success: Linux 3.10 and 3.13 '408 passed', macOS 3.10 and 3.13 '406 passed, 2 skipped' (the two skips are not row tests and give their reasons). The run just before on main (45084816300, d8244028, the plan only) had 405 and '403 passed, 2 skipped': three more tests ran on every system, the gate's three new tests. No job listed a row's test as not run here. The logs use pytest -q, so they give counts, not names. Before the merge, a real row's test moved six ways where it cannot run, each in a throwaway copy, made the gate fail all six, and removing each of its guards made that guard's test fail.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, in a sister Windstorm skill, not in Pit Board: its plugin manifest named an old version through three releases, so on a stock machine `claude plugin update` said it was already at the latest version and kept the old code, and a person never got the fixes; a control with only the label changed updated at once. Checked here the same night: tag v0.1.1 and main named one version in every place, but a test held only plugin.json against __version__, not the CHANGELOG's heading, and nothing checked a tag's labels against its name.
rows.promise: One version in every place: plugin.json, __version__ and CHANGELOG.md's top dated heading name the same version, and a not-yet-released heading above it names a later one; the suite fails when one differs. Run in a fresh clone of a release tag, before the marketplace pin moves, the suite refuses the tag unless its name equals every version label in it.
rows.proven: 2026-11-22, CI's own logs on main (GitHub's hosted runners, Linux and macOS, Python 3.10 and 3.13): run 45099512523 on the merge commit a214d865 completed with success, and its log names 'tests/test_g21_versions.py::test_G21_1_one_version_in_every_place PASSED' in all four jobs (Linux '413 passed', macOS '411 passed, 2 skipped', the two skips the G10.5 wrapper cases with their reason). That checkout names 0.1.1 in plugin.json, __version__ and the top dated CHANGELOG heading, under the not-yet-released 0.1.2. The tag check was seen to pass in a fresh clone of the real v0.1.1 and to refuse a v0.1.2 tag put on main's commit in a throwaway clone; it runs for a real release tag first at 0.1.2's fresh-clone step.

declined.heard: 2026-11-21, the M1 pilot: the pitboard command on the agent's PATH is the pilot marketplace's source folder, not the version folder the hooks run from.
declined.why: Only a directory (local) marketplace has a source folder to put on PATH. In the pilot both copies were the same commit, and both go through the G21.4 launcher. M2a installs from the GitHub marketplace, and the first M2a lane checks which folder is on PATH there. If it differs from the hooks' folder, this becomes a row.
